findings.quote: and on-demand is cheaper only when utilization is [below 35%](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-ondemand-cheaper-below-35-percent-utilization).

findings.quote: On-demand is not always cheaper: it costs less when the average use of provisioned capacity would be [below 35%](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-ondemand-cheaper-below-35-percent-utilization).

findings.quote: For rarely read data, the **table class** DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (Standard-IA) suits tables where [storage is the dominant cost](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-table-class-standard-ia-lower-storage-cost).

The chapter states only the storage side; the 'but not if' (read- or write-heavy table) that decides a Standard-IA question is never taught, and Question 18 does not mention it either. findings.quote: In an Aurora global database, [only the primary cluster performs write operations](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-vs-aurora-global-database-single-writer), so the clusters in Europe and Asia cannot accept local writes.
findings.evidence: The same fact's qualifier records the exception: 'Aurora write forwarding lets secondary clusters send writes to the primary'. With write forwarding a secondary cluster does accept the write, but the write still travels to the primary Region, so the latency requirement still fails. 'cannot accept local writes' is a claim she may contradict from memory and then distrust the key. Say: 'only the primary cluster performs writes, so every write from Europe and Asia still travels to the primary Region.' In the same question, the Why-not of option A begins 'It works,' although the stem requires every write to be served in the user's own Region; say 'It keeps the slow writes'. Needs q add --replace and a new blind round.
findings.resolution: fix-28: q022 option b why as claims-15; option a why now begins 'It keeps the slow writes:' instead of 'It works'. Explanation-only edits; stem, options and key unchanged.
